title: BSP 2021 Financial Inclusion Survey (public source)
summary: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas' nationally representative survey of Filipino adults on accounts, savings, loans, payments and digital access, with supporting focus groups and interviews. Reference year 2021.
label_notes: Labelled by reading the PDF. Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes (the report's own page numbers differ). Method is 'mixed' because the report pairs the survey with FGDs and IDIs; every finding below is from the survey. sample_size is the survey sample; base_n is left empty where the report gives only a share of adults as the base.

findings.text: 56% of Filipino adults had a formal account in 2021, up from 29% in 2019.
findings.quote: Account penetration significantly increased to 56% in 2021 from 29% in

findings.text: 36% of Filipino adults had an e-money account in 2021, up from 8% in 2019, making e-money the most-owned type of account.
findings.quote: percentage of Filipinos with e-money account grew more than four times to 36% in 2021

findings.text: Among adults aged 30-39, 65% had an account, more than twice the 27% of adults aged 15-19.
findings.quote: the share of adults aged 30 to 39 years old with an account (65%) was more than twice that of younger adults aged 15 to 19 years old (27%)

findings.text: Lack of documentary requirements was cited by 40% of unbanked adults as a reason for not having an account, second to not having enough money (45%).
findings.quote: Lack of enough money and lack of documentary requirements were the topmost reasons for not having an account, as reported by 45% and 40% of the unbanked, respectively

findings.text: 54% of unbanked adults were unaware of the basic deposit account, the BSP's low-cost account designed to address cost and document barriers.
findings.quote: 54% of unbanked adults were still unaware of the basic deposit account (BDA)

findings.text: 45% of Filipino adults had an outstanding loan in 2021, up from 33% in 2019; family and friends were the most common source.
findings.quote: the share of adults with outstanding loans jumped to 45%, from 33% in 2019

findings.text: Only 4% of borrowers took their loans from banks in 2021, barely up from 3% in 2019.
findings.quote: the share of borrowers sourcing their loans from banks only stood at four percent (4%) in 2021
